questions.question: For the best protection, wear a helmet that:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no obvious damage.

questions.question: Which surface gives the best grip for a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce grip for tires. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates in the road are all more dangerous for motorcycles than dry pavement.

questions.question: A leather jacket:

options.text: Can make a rider look cool.
Is usually too warm to wear when riding.
Should not be worn when riding.

questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved jacket, preferably leather, when riding. In warm weather, a leather jacket can protect you from dehydration. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool even in hot weather.

questions.question: When choosing a protective jacket or pants, look for:
questions.explanation: Wear long pants and a jacket to cover your arms and legs fully when riding. Leather clothing provides the most protection.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Look ahead and prepare for possible hazards.
Focus on the controls and speedometer instead of the road.
Not worry about hazards because they are rare.
Look ahead but avoid looking for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and prepare for possible hazards.
questions.explanation: Always look well ahead to spot possible hazards early. This helps you react before you reach them.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. Follow the rules posted on these signs.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should:

options.text: Stay in the same lane position all the time.
Constantly move between lane positions to keep other drivers away.
Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Adjust your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: Which material offers the best protection for motorcyclists?
questions.explanation: Leather provides the most protection for motorcyclists. Always wear clothing that covers your legs and arms completely when riding.

questions.question: When riding at night, do all of the following except:

options.text: Use headlights from cars ahead to see the road better.
Increase your distance from other vehicles.
Use your high beam headlight when appropriate.

questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance to avoid crashes. Use headlights from vehicles ahead to see farther. Be flexible with lane position at night. Use your high beams when not following or meeting other vehicles.

questions.question: As a motorcycle operator, you can help others see you by:
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright clothing, use your headlight at all times, and use your turn signals.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a dangerously slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible over the slippery surface.

questions.question: What is the proper body position on a motorcycle?

options.text: Sit forward enough that your arms bend slightly when holding the handle grips.
Sit as far back as possible and stretch to reach the handle grips.
Lean over the bike so your arms hold you up.
Keep your knees far from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit forward enough that your arms bend slightly when holding the handle grips.
questions.explanation: Sit forward enough that your arms bend slightly when holding the handle grips. This lets you reach and operate the controls easily and comfortably.

questions.question: What can you do to be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Swerve within your lane to get attention.

questions.explanation: Use your headlight and position your motorcycle in the lane where oncoming traffic can see you best. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can take action to avoid danger.

questions.question: What must you have when carrying a passenger on a motorcycle?

options.text: A seat large enough for two riders.
The passenger should not wear protective clothing.
A sticker on the brake light to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: A seat large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have a seat large enough for two riders and footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear as you.

questions.question: What is the best source of information about your motorcycle?

options.text: Someone who rides a different type of motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle.

questions.question: Who is most likely to crash?

options.text: Those who have completed a safety course.

questions.explanation: Beginning riders who lack training and are unfamiliar with their motorcycle are most likely to crash.

questions.question: How does maintaining a cushion of space help when riding?

options.text: It gives you time to react to hazards.
It hides you from other drivers.
It prevents you from avoiding hazards.
It allows you to look at road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. You need this space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: Which fabric gives motorcycle riders the best protection?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: What type of footwear is best for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots or high shoes that support your ankles provide the best protection. Lace them securely and tuck any loose laces away before riding.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: How long does a pre-ride inspection usually take?

options.text: A few minutes. Do it once a month.
A few minutes. Do it before every ride.
Over an hour. A mechanic must do it.
Over an hour. Only do it if you carry a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes. Do it before every ride.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-ride inspection before every ride. It takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider improve visibility?
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing with reflective materials so other drivers can see you. Always use your headlight and signals.

questions.question: Before mounting a motorcycle, which item do you NOT need to check?
questions.explanation: Check tire pressure and tread, oil and fluids, and lights and signals before riding. Paint damage is not a safety concern.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding directly alongside another vehicle?

options.text: You may be in its blind spot.
Other drivers may need the lane.
You cannot see what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside a vehicle puts you in its blind spot. The driver cannot see you, and the vehicle may block your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: When riding, what should you do?

options.text: Focus only on the road directly ahead.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: Look through turns by turning only your head and eyes, not your shoulders. Bend your arms slightly on the handgrips. Keep your knees against the tank for balance. Watch for hazards ahead, behind, and to the sides.
